subproblem.title: Successive determinantal ideals are decreasing
subproblem.statement: Let R be a commutative ring, let ι and κ be finite types, let P be an ι-by-κ matrix over R, and let d be a natural number. Define D_a(P) as the ideal generated by determinants of submatrices selected by embeddings Fin a into the row and column sets. Then D_(d+1)(P) is contained in D_d(P), including d=0 and unavailable sizes.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {ι κ : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] (P : Matrix ι κ R) (d : ℕ), (Ideal.span {x : R | ∃ (rows : Fin (d + 1) ↪ ι) (cols : Fin (d + 1) ↪ κ), x = Matrix.det (P.submatrix rows cols)}) ≤ Ideal.span {x : R | ∃ (rows : Fin d ↪ ι) (cols : Fin d ↪ κ), x = Matrix.det (P.submatrix rows cols)}
subproblem.natural_proof:
1. Denote the two determinantal ideals by D_(d+1)(P) and D_d(P). It suffices to put every generating (d+1)-minor in D_d(P); if there are no such minors the source ideal is zero.
2. Fix row and column embeddings ρ and γ from Fin(d+1), and put C=P[ρ,γ]. Expand det C along row 0. The term indexed by j∈Fin(d+1) is (-1)^j C(0,j) times the determinant obtained by deleting row 0 and column j.
3. The remaining row selection is i↦ρ(i+1), and the remaining column selection is γ composed with the increasing map from Fin d that skips j. Both maps are injective, being composites of injective maps. Thus each cofactor determinant is a generator of D_d(P). Each signed entry times that determinant belongs to D_d(P), as does their finite sum.
4. This proves the desired containment of spans. For d=0 the cofactor is the empty determinant 1 with its unique empty selections, so the same argument applies without a positivity assumption.
proof_key_steps: Reduce the ideal containment to a single generating minor.
Expand a (d+1)-determinant along its first row.
Identify each cofactor with a d-minor using composed embeddings.
Use closure under scalar multiplication and finite sums, including empty cofactors.

audit.reason: The one-line type exactly states the claimed containment with all hypotheses. Expansion along row zero produces precisely the d-minors described by the composed injective selections. Ideal closure proves containment, including d=0 and unavailable sizes. The proof is complete and independent of the parent and other children.
